faq.title: Pricing FAQ
faq.q1: Wait — it's really free? No hidden catch?
faq.a1: Yes. Lead Machine is MIT-licensed open source. You can download it, run it, modify it, sell derivatives, all for free, forever. The project is maintained by volunteers who use it daily.
faq.q2: Why don't you charge subscriptions like everyone else?
faq.a2: Because the whole point of Lead Machine is to kill the €200/mo SaaS stack for freelancers. Charging would defeat the mission. We make money by selling custom builds & consulting, not by nickel-and-diming users.
faq.q3: What about BYOK — are my keys safe?
faq.a3: Your keys are encrypted client-side with AES-GCM 256-bit using PBKDF2 with 100,000 iterations, keyed to your browser fingerprint, and stored only in YOUR localStorage. They are NEVER sent to any server in plaintext. You can verify the crypto.ts code on GitHub.
faq.q4: Can I self-host on Vercel / Fly.io / Coolify?
faq.a4: Yes — see the Deploy docs. For Vercel, attach a persistent volume for SQLite (or switch to Postgres — single DATABASE_URL change).
faq.q5: Is there a hosted managed version?
faq.a5: Not currently, but the community is working on one. Star & watch the repo for updates.

byok.title: BYOK & Zero-Knowledge Architecture
byok.subtitle: We built Lead Machine so we would trust it ourselves. Here is exactly how your secrets stay yours.

crypto.p1: All API keys you paste into Lead Machine (Gemini, Groq, SMTP user/pass) are encrypted in your browser BEFORE anything else happens.
crypto.p2: We use the browser's native Web Crypto API — zero third-party crypto libraries. The implementation is auditable in lib/crypto.ts.
crypto.step1: A 16-byte cryptographically-random salt is generated per payload (crypto.getRandomValues).
crypto.step2: A 12-byte random IV (initialization vector) is generated per encryption — non-repeating, GCM-compliant.
crypto.step3: Your browser fingerprint (UA+lang+platform+resolution+timezone+cores+memory) is used as the passphrase.
crypto.step4: PBKDF2 with SHA-256 stretches that passphrase over 100,000 iterations into a 256-bit AES key.
crypto.step5: AES-GCM 256 encrypts your keys. The auth tag is included in the ciphertext (GCM property).
crypto.step6: Salt + IV + ciphertext + iteration count are base64-encoded and JSON-stringified. Result stored ONLY in your localStorage.

zeroknowledge.p1: “Zero knowledge” in Lead Machine means: by design, the server infrastructure physically cannot access your keys, your leads, or your business data.
zeroknowledge.p2: There is no middleman. There is no proxy. There is no “our servers call the AI for you”. The browser calls Gemini/Groq/Nodemailer directly — or, if you self-host on your laptop, your Node process calls them from YOUR IP address.
zeroknowledge.prom1: We NEVER receive or log API keys in plaintext. Never. Impossible.
zeroknowledge.prom2: We NEVER send your leads, contacts or quote data to third-party servers.
zeroknowledge.prom3: We NEVER include tracking scripts (no GA, no Meta, no Pixel, no Segment, no Sentry by default).
zeroknowledge.prom4: We NEVER sell or share data with anyone — we don't have any to share.
zeroknowledge.prom5: All of the above is verifiable by reading the MIT-licensed source on GitHub. If you find otherwise, it's a bug — email axsen_kurtoski@financier.com for bounty.

transparency.title: Full Transparency Report
transparency.subtitle: Lead Machine is an open book. Here is what we do, don't do, and why.

sections.dataBody:
If you run Lead Machine on your laptop (the recommended way for individual users): ZERO. We receive nothing, we store nothing, we process nothing. Every byte lives in your prisma/dev.db SQLite file.

If you use a public community demo instance (not operated by the Lead Machine project directly) or a custom managed build operated by a third party: that operator's data policies apply. The Lead Machine open-source codebase itself does not phone home.
sections.cookiesTitle: Cookies — only the strictly necessary ones
sections.cookiesBody:
We set 3 first-party functional cookies and nothing else:

next-intl-locale — 1 year — remembers your language preference.
lm_license — 10 years — reserved cookie name for future optional OSS enterprise features. 100% NOT SET in the current open-source release.
lm_consent — 90 days — remembers that you saw the cookie banner.

That's it. No Google Analytics. No Meta Pixel. No LinkedIn Insight. No Hotjar. No third-party cookies. Nada.
sections.opensourceBody: Every line of code that ships in Lead Machine is on GitHub under the MIT license. The build is reproducible. Dependency trees are pinned (package-lock.json). If you can read TypeScript, you can verify every claim on this page.
sections.securityBody: Rate limiting on every write endpoint. Input sanitization on every param. Settings whitelist (mass-injection impossible). Secrets redacted from server responses. Prisma transactions + batch ops (no partial writes). CSP-friendly by default. See SECURITY.md for full policy and vulnerability disclosure process.
sections.financialBody: Lead Machine is a labor of love, not a SaaS business. Revenue comes from three channels: (1) custom development for agencies who need bespoke CRM fields or integrations, (2) deployment & security consulting for self-hosted teams, (3) optional GitHub Sponsors from users who want to tip. No subscriptions. No VC funding. No growth targets that would force us to compromise on privacy.

deploy.title: Deploy Lead Machine anywhere
deploy.subtitle: Run on your laptop in 3 commands, or deploy to any VPS/serverless platform.

local.title: Laptop (Recommended)
steps: cd lead-machine && npm install && npm run setup
local.notes: Zero config. SQLite file at prisma/dev.db. Works offline.

vps.title: VPS / VM (Caddy + Basic Auth)
steps: Spin up a $5/mo VPS (Ubuntu 22.04, 1GB RAM minimum)
Install Node 20 LTS. Clone repo, npm ci, npm run setup
Run behind Caddy with automatic HTTPS + basic_auth
vps.notes: Daily SQLite backup via cron + rclone to S3-compatible storage.

serverless.title: Serverless (Vercel / Fly.io)
steps: Fork the repo, connect to Vercel / Fly.io
Attach persistent volume for SQLite OR swap DATABASE_URL to Postgres
serverless.notes: ⚠️ Vercel ephemeral FS — you MUST mount a volume or use Postgres for durable storage.

collected.title: 2. Categories of Data Collected
collected.body:
Lead Machine collects the absolute minimum of personal data. In practice, only the following:

a) Contact form data: if you voluntarily fill in a contact form (demo request, partnership, bug report, waitlist), we collect the name and email address you provide. Processing is based solely on your explicit, opt-in consent.

b) Server logs: our web hosts (Vercel, GitHub Pages) may retain transient IP-based connection logs for up to 7 days for pure security/anti-abuse purposes. We do not have access to these logs unless a legal request compels the host to provide them.

c) We explicitly do NOT collect:
— Third-party analytics (no Google Analytics, no GA4, no Matomo, no Plausible)
— Advertising or marketing tracking cookies (no Meta Pixel, no LinkedIn Insight, no Twitter/X Ads)
— User behavioral profiling of any kind
— Cross-device tracking
— Financial data (we don't process payments)

purposes.title: 3. Purposes of Processing
purposes.body:
The Data Controller processes personal data solely for the following purposes:

— Responding to contact requests: when you email us or submit a form, we use your data to reply. Period.
— Security & anti-abuse: transient IP logs processed by our hosting providers solely to prevent DDoS, brute-force attacks and spam.
— Compliance with a legal obligation: where we are compelled by binding EU or national law to produce records.

basis.title: 4. Legal Basis for Processing
basis.body:
Processing is based on one or more of the following, as applicable under Art. 6 GDPR:

(a) Explicit, specific, revocable consent (Art. 6(1)(a)) — for contact form submissions and waitlist signups. You may withdraw consent at any time by emailing axsen_kurtoski@financier.com.

(b) Compliance with a legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)) — e.g., tax record retention.

(c) Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)) — only in the narrow case of server-level anti-abuse/security logs. We balance these interests against your rights and find the impact to be minimal (transient, unprofiled, never used for marketing).

retention.title: 5. Data Retention
retention.body:
Data categories are retained for the following maximum periods:

— Contact form submissions (name + email): 36 months from the last interaction with you. This allows us to recognize returning conversations. After 36 months, we permanently delete.

— Transient host-level security logs: up to 7 days (outside our control).

— Financial/customer records relating to consulting or custom builds: 10 years per Italian civil & tax law (Art. 2220 c.c., Art. 3 D.P.R. 600/1973).

rights.title: 6. Your Rights (GDPR Articles 15–22)
rights.body:
Under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (and comparable laws like the CCPA), you have the following rights, free of charge:

— Right of access (Art. 15): you may request confirmation of whether we process your data and obtain a copy.
— Right to rectification (Art. 16): correct inaccurate or incomplete data.
— Right to erasure (“right to be forgotten”, Art. 17): request deletion, subject to legal retention exceptions.
— Right to restriction (Art. 18): suspend processing in certain cases.
— Right to data portability (Art. 20): receive your data in a machine-readable format.
— Right to object (Art. 21): object to processing based on legitimate interests.
— Right to withdraw consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing based on consent before withdrawal.
— Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.

How to exercise: email axsen_kurtoski@financier.com with the subject “GDPR Request”. We respond within 30 calendar days.
